text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a p95 token-latency spike on the token dashboard for eu-west-1 starting ~07:12 UTC. TTFT went from ~220ms to ~420ms for a 10-minute window. Grafana panel: /d/redwood/tokendash?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west-1
rob: Ugh. Any idea if it's traffic-related (tokens/sec) or a backend regression? Can you paste the panel queries?
maya: Initial look: tokens/sec steady, so not pure traffic. Panels use histogram_quantile on per-request latency buckets and a recording rule for ttft_seconds. Here's the query I was looking at:
```promql
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference",region="eu-west-1"}[2m])) by (le, model, instance))
```
And tokens/sec per model: 
```promql
sum(rate(redwood_tokens_processed_total{region="eu-west-1"}[1m])) by (model)
```
rob: That histogram query might be noisy on short windows. Also if KV cache miss rate jumped it'd increase p95 without tokens/sec change. Do we have a cache_hit_ratio metric?
sasha: We do: redwood_kv_cache_hits_total / redwood_kv_cache_requests_total as an instant. I just checked — hit ratio for the affected model dropped from 0.87 -> 0.52 at 07:10-07:20. That aligns.
maya: Good catch. So likely KV cache thrash after a restart or scaling event. Any recent node restarts in that AZ?
jordan: Autoscaler had a burst scale event at 07:05:12 due to a different customer workload. Kube events show 3 pods cycled in eu-west-1 around 07:06-07:09. Could explain cache warmup.
rob: That means our alert should ignore short warmups. Current paged alert fires on p95 > 300ms for 5m. We probably need to correlate with cache_hit_ratio or require sustained tokens/sec or combine with pod_restarts. Proposal: change alert to use a for: 15m and add an annotation pointing to the cache hit panel.
sasha: Or make alert more specific: alert if p95 > 300ms for 10m AND cache_hit_ratio < 0.7 for 10m AND tokens/sec > 50. That will reduce noise from low-traffic spikes.
alerts-bot: incident-notify: Alert "HighTokenP95Latency" triggered for eu-west-1 at 07:14 UTC. Notified on-call.
maya: I also want a drilldown link from the main p95 panel that filters by model and instance so on-call can immediately see if it's a cache miss vs kernel slowdown. Grafana variables currently: region, model, instance, quantile.
rob: Agree. Also add a recording rule for p95 to avoid re-evaluating histogram_quantile over many series in alerts: e.g. record: redwood_latency_p95_seconds
```promql
record: redwood_latency_p95_seconds
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, instance))
```
That reduces alert CPU and stabilizes values.
sasha: +1. We should also tag the recording rule with 'slo:true' so dashboards can pick it up.
jordan: Ops action items: 1) Update alert to composite rule (p95 + cache ratio + tokens/sec) with 10m for testing. 2) Add recording rule for p95/p99. 3) Add dashboard drilldown for model/instance and link to Loki logs for that instance. 4) Run a backtest on last 90 days to ensure we don't accidentally suppress real regressions.
maya: I'll own 1 & 3. rob, can you own recording rules?
rob: Yep I'll PR the rules to monitoring repo today and add unit tests for the recording expressions.
sasha: For backtest: we should run the alert over historical data and compute false positive/false negative rates. I can write a quick script to evaluate the new composite alert logic against past incidents.
maya: Nice. Also one more tweak: our current TTFT panel uses moving average which smooths p95 peaks away. For SLOs we want a rolling 5m p95 line plus raw p95 points. Add both to the panel.
jordan: Noted. Let's also add costs note: token processing cost spikes during warmups were negligible but if this becomes frequent autoscaler churn will increase GPU spin-up costs. Keep an eye.
maya: Ok I'll open threads: - PR for alert rule change (link will be added) - Dashboard edit for drilldown and TTFT lines - Incident follow-up summary after we stabilize
rob: Thanks. If anyone sees recurring cache thrash we should consider sticky warm caches or node draining strategy change to minimize simultaneous pod cycles.
sasha: Filing a follow-up task for a safer rollout policy for autoscaler, assigning to infra team.
maya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
